If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For less urgent cases, contact a poison control center. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. 4. This medication is prescribed specifically for your current condition. Discard any unused medication once your treatment is complete. 5. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 6. Store this medication at room temperature. Discard the solution if it changes color, becomes cloudy, or develops particles. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly dispose of expired or unused products. 7. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs. 8. Temporary stinging or burning of the eyes may occur when this medication is applied. Other possible side effects include blurred vision, eye discomfort, itching, redness, dryness, tearing, a sensation of a foreign object in the eye, or sensitivity to light. 9. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to a new fungal eye infection. Do not use it for longer than prescribed. 10. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, if you experience symptoms of a severe allergic reaction, seek medical attention immediately. 11. Before using ofloxacin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other quinolones (e.g., ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as preservatives like benzalkonium chloride, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. 12. After applying this medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred or unstable. Avoid activities requiring clear vision, such as driving, until your vision stabilizes. 13. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. 14.
